pamphlet_excerpts: Hazards, First Aid & Safety: In rowing, blisters are most likely to occur on the hands (p. 13).
Hazards, First Aid & Safety Principle 2: Pay attention to any tender or sensitive areas (hot spots) that indicate the start of a blister (p. 13).

step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): If you do get a blister, cover and protect the area from further irritation (p. 13).
Step 2 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): A sprain occurs when an ankle, wrist, or other joint is bent farenough to over stretch the ligaments, the tough bands that hold joints together (p. 13).
Step 3 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): A strain occurs when muscles are over stretched, creating tears in the muscle fibers (p. 13).
Step 4 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): Minor sprains and strains cause only mild discomfort, but more serious sprains and strains might be temporarily disabling (p. 13).

step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (BSA Swimmer Qualification Check): To qualify as a "swimmer," you must pass the following swimmer test (p. 15).
Step 2 (BSA Swimmer Qualification Check): Jump feet first into water over your head in depth (p. 15).
Step 3 (BSA Swimmer Qualification Check): Level off and swim 75 yards in a strong manner using one or more of the following strokes: sidestroke, breaststroke, trudgen, or crawl (p. 15).
Step 4 (BSA Swimmer Qualification Check): Then swim 25 yards using an easy resting backstroke (p. 15).

pamphlet_excerpts: Alone in A Rowboat Push: If you are with a friend and your boat capsizes, pull yourself up over the side of the swamped boat while your friend holds down the other side (p. 65).
Alone in A Rowboat Push Principle 2: Push down on the gunwale with both hands so that you bring yourself up to where your hips are about level with the gunwale (p. 65).
Alone in A Rowboat Push Principle 3: Then roll over so that you fall into the bottom of the swamped boat, landing on your backside (p. 65).
Alone in A Rowboat Push Principle 4: You can then lean over the side to counterbalance as your friend follows the same steps to come in over the opposite side (p. 65).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Alone in A Rowboat Push): Remember that when you pull yourself up on the gunwale, the gunwale will be forced down into the water (p. 65).
Step 2 (Alone in A Rowboat Push): After you roll in and get your weightoff the gunwale, it will rise back (p. 65).
Step 3 (Alone in A Rowboat Push): Even when fully awash, the gunwale of most boats will be a few inches above the level of the water (p. 65).
Step 4 (Alone in A Rowboat Push): If you are alone and your boat swamps and yougo over the side, the best way toget back in is over the transom (p. 65).
